questions.q: State Newton's three laws of motion and explain the concept of inertia.

answer.text: Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion. The mass of an object is a measure of its inertia, so a heavier object is harder to start or stop.
An object remains at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an unbalanced force; this is also called the law of inertia.
The force acting on an object equals its mass times its acceleration, written as F equals m a, and is the rate of change of momentum. The SI unit of force is the newton.
To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, the two forces acting on different bodies.

questions.q: What is momentum, and state the law of conservation of momentum with an example.

answer.text: Momentum is the product of the mass of an object and its velocity. It is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, and its SI unit is the kilogram metre per second. A heavy, fast-moving body has large momentum and is hard to stop.
The law of conservation of momentum states that, in the absence of any external force, the total momentum of a system of bodies remains constant.

When a gun is fired, the bullet moves forward with a certain momentum, and the gun recoils backward with an equal momentum in the opposite direction, so that the total momentum stays zero. The same principle explains how rockets are propelled.

questions.q: How does Newton's second law of motion explain everyday experiences of force?

answer.text: states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of the force — giving the familiar relation force equals mass times acceleration.

list: A greater force produces a greater acceleration for the same mass
A heavier object needs a greater force to gain the same acceleration

answer.text: The law is at work all around us.

list: A cricketer pulls back the hands while catching a ball to increase the time and reduce the force felt
This is why falling on a hard floor hurts more than falling on a mattress

questions.q: How does Newton's third law of motion apply to the recoil of a gun and the motion of a rocket?

answer.text: states that to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, and these forces act on two different bodies.

list: When the gun pushes the bullet forward (action), the bullet pushes the gun backward (reaction), so the gun recoils
The gun's larger mass gives it a much smaller backward velocity
It pushes hot gases downward, and the gases push the rocket upward with an equal and opposite force
